name: Victorian millinery
summary: The women's hats and bonnets of Queen Victoria's reign. A wire and buckram frame carried silk, velvet, felt or straw, trimmed by hand with ribbon, flowers and feathers. The shape followed the dress, from deep poke bonnet to small tilted hat.

philosophy.core_thesis: A hat completes a lady's dress, and the trim shows the skill of the milliner.
design_principles: Build the shape on a wire and buckram frame, then cover it with cloth cut on the bias.
Cut the brim of a poke bonnet 8 to 12 cm deep in the 1840s, so that the face looks out of a tunnel.
Shrink the bonnet to a small hat at the back of the head by the 1860s, as the hair is dressed higher.
Tie the strings under the chin in a silk bow 4 to 6 cm wide.
Mass the trim at one side or at the front: flowers, ribbon loops, a plume or a bird.
Match the cloth of the trim to the dress of the wearer.
Use felt for winter, silk for the evening and plaited straw for summer.
Sew the lining and the head band by hand.
anti_patterns: A bare hat with no trim
A flat crown in the modern shape
Sports felt, baseball caps and visors

silhouette.shape: A small frame that stands high or far forward on smooth hair, with the trim massed at one side.
silhouette.line: A curved brim line that frames the face, and a crown that slopes back to the nape.
silhouette.fit: The hat perches on the head and is held by ribbon strings under the chin or by a long hat pin.
silhouette.proportion: Poke brim 8–12 cm deep in the 1840s; bonnet width 20–24 cm; crown 8–10 cm high; trim up to half the height of the hat.
rules: Frame the face with the brim, and keep the hair smooth under it.
Shorten the brim and raise the crown as the decades pass, until the bonnet is a small hat in the 1870s.
Place the main trim at the front or at one side, never at the centre back.
Fill the space between the brim and the cheek with a ruche of tulle or lace.

fabrics.rule: Cover a stiff frame with a cloth that takes a bias fold. Use felt and velvet for winter, taffeta and satin for dress, tulle and lace for the evening.

methods: felt steamed and blocked on a wooden block
construction.closures: Ribbon strings tied under the chin, or a long hat pin through the crown.
construction.details: A ruche of tulle at the brim edge, a curtain at the nape and a bow at the side. Flowers, a plume or a bird trim the crown.

surface.pattern: Plain cloth in one colour with a contrast trim; a check or stripe in the ribbon; jet beads on the mourning bonnet.
surface.gloss: Velvet and felt at 2–6 GU; silk taffeta and satin at 30–60 GU.
surface.wear: A new, crisp trim is the aim; sun fades silk, and a limp bow or a crushed brim ends the life of the hat.

palette.strategy: One main colour for the hat, taken from the dress, with a trim in a contrast or a tone close to it; black for mourning.

making.scale: A milliner's workshop made each hat to order; from the 1860s, drapers and department stores also sold trimmed hats ready made.
making.signs: Hand stitches in the lining, a wire edge, and trim that is sewn on and not glued.

pieces.form: Poke bonnet with a deep brim and ribbon strings
Small tilted hat with a velvet crown and a plume
Felt walking hat with a ribbon band and a bow
Evening bonnet with a ruche of tulle and silk flowers
Wedding bonnet in satin with a lace veil

positive: museum photograph on a hat stand

emotion.target_response: A sense of modest grace and of care: the hat frames the face and shows the work of the milliner.

use_cases: a costume brief for a Victorian drama
a hat design study or a museum label
a fashion image prompt for an 1860s woman
avoid_when: the brief is a hat for sport or for the street today
the brief wants a simple unlined cap

modifiers.how: Pair the hat with a full skirt cut in the same cloth, and keep the trim and the ribbon strings.
Cover the hat in black crape and add jet beads; drop the bright flowers.
Cut the brim away, shrink the crown to a close cap and drop the trim to one small bow.

ornament_level.note: A plain walking hat has one bow; an evening bonnet carries flowers, lace and beads.
